title: Authorization grid, resource affinity, and admin guardrails
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design and implement the next-generation RBAC v2 authorization model focused on: a compact authorization grid (permission expression language + sparse matrix), resource affinity (grouped resource boundaries for tenant and sub-tenant), and operational admin guardrails (breakglass, scoped elevation, and emergency deny). Deliverables: schema, permission resolver algorithm, audit hooks, SSO/SAML attribute mappings, and a rollout plan with migration tooling.
background: Current RBAC has grown ad-hoc with flat roles and tenant-wide bindings. Multiple incidents showed confusion around privilege escalation and lack of fine-grained audit metadata. We need a formal model that supports delegation, temporary elevation, and predictable decision precedence while keeping decision latency low for the runtime.
goals: 1) Define an expressive but bounded permission expression language that supports allow/deny, resource-anchored scopes, and temporal elevation. 2) Produce a sparse permission matrix representation for fast evaluation and compact storage. 3) Specify admin guardrails and emergency flows that are auditable. 4) Integrate SSO/SAML attributes for role assignment automation. 5) Add minimal runtime hooks for high-fidelity audit logs.
non_goals: Replace existing tenant isolation or multi-cluster networking. Full ABAC policy engine (e.g., OPA style) is out of scope; we aim for pragmatic expressiveness tailored to Redwood product needs.
scope: Schema for RoleSets, Bindings, Scopes, and PermissionExpressions; permission resolution algorithm and pseudocode; database representation for sparse matrix; audit event contract; SSO attribute mapping guide; migration tool design; tests and canary rollout.
decision_log:
- Adopt role-set composition (role sets can include other role sets with explicit deny precedence).
- PermissionExpressions will be sized to at most 4 predicates to keep evaluation O(1) in practice.
- Deny wins over allow when resource scope intersects.
- Temporary elevations use a token with TTL and revocation list; breakglass generates high-fidelity audit events and requires 2FA confirmation for enterprise accounts.
permission_expression_summary: Syntax: <verb>:<resource-pattern>[@scope][#condition]. Examples: 'read:dataset/*@tenant:123', 'write:deployment/*@env:prod#owner!=requester'. The expression language supports wildcarding, explicit resource IDs, and a limited set of attribute equality/inequality checks.
permission_matrix_sample:
Columns: roleSetId, permissionExpression, effect(allow|deny), resourceAffinity, temporalPolicy
Row example 1: analytics-reader, 'read:embedding/*@tenant:*', allow, affinity=[dataset:high], none
Row example 2: infra-deployer, 'write:deployment/*@env:prod', deny, affinity=[cluster:critical], emergency-elevation-allowed
Row example 3: support-jenkins, 'read:logs/*@tenant:{owned}', allow, affinity=[log-store:standard], ttl-30m
resource_hierarchy_outline: Platform -> Organization -> Project -> Environment -> ResourceType (dataset, model, deployment) -> ResourceID. Scopes bind at any node; nearest-binding precedence resolves conflicts. Resource affinity groups resources for batching of permissions and rate-limited admin operations.
admin_guardrails:
- Scoped breakglass tokens with just-in-time elevation and mandatory reason.
- Auto-revocation on policy change or 2FA reset.
- Force audit and alerting for any allow that used a breakglass token.
- Soft deny mode (log-only) for first 2 weeks after role migration.
- Emergency global deny switch (SRE-runbook) with audit reason and mandatory postmortem.
audit_logging_requirements: Every authorization decision must emit a structured audit event with: timestamp, actor, effective_role_set, evaluated_expressions (list), decision, reason, resource_path, request_id, trace_id, evaluated_cache_hit(bool), and optional breakglass_token_id. Retention: 13 months for enterprise customers, 90 days for self-serve. Events must be exportable to SIEM and support gRPC/HTTP bulk ingest.
sso_saml_considerations: Map SAML attributes to roleSets and ephemeral scopes where possible (e.g., SAML attribute 'x-redwood-role': 'analytics-reader;ttl=3600'). Support SCIM provisioning for long-lived bindings. For SSO-initiated breakglass, require AAD conditional access confirmation. Document attribute mapping patterns and fallback when attributes are missing.
implementation_plan: 1) Schema proposal and review (this ticket) -> 2) Prototype resolver in auth-service (feature flag) -> 3) Storage adaptor for sparse matrix (Postgres + tiled index) -> 4) Audit hook implementation and export -> 5) SSO/SAML attribute connector updates -> 6) Migration tool to translate existing flat roles to roleSets -> 7) Canary rollout to internal teams -> 8) Gradual customer rollout with soft deny and opt-in.
rollout_steps:
- Stage 1: Schema and resolver behind feature flag in staging.
- Stage 2: Internal-only canary (platform + infra teams) for 2 weeks.
- Stage 3: Opt-in beta for 5 customers with varied tenancy models.
- Stage 4: Soft deny/default logging migration for all customers (2 weeks).
- Stage 5: Enforcement on by default and deprecate legacy bindings after 30 days.
testing_plan: Unit tests for permission parsing and evaluation, property tests for precedence rules, integration tests with SSO/SAML providers (Okta, AAD), load tests to keep auth latency < 2ms median, and e2e authorization flow tests including audit events verification.
risk_mitigation:
- Keep legacy resolver as fallback for 90 days.
- Soft-deny mode for initial migrations to detect unintended permission revocations.
- Implement feature-flagged per-organization rollout so we can quickly revert.
- Add synthetic traffic checks to alert on unexpected drops in successful auth decisions.
open_questions: What is the upper bound on number of roleSets per tenant before we require sharding?
Should resource affinity be persisted as a first-class DB column for indexing?
What's the canonical format for embedding evaluated_expressions in audit (string vs structured array)?
Is 'deny wins' acceptable in all tenant models or should some customers be allowed 'allow wins' with explicit contract?
notes: Prototype on branch feature/authz-grid has a working resolver for simple patterns.
Aligned with legal on audit retention for enterprise customers.
SRE wants emergency global deny to bypass cache and hit DB directly.
updates: 2026-03-03: Initial proposal posted for architecture review.
2026-03-06: Meeting with SRE and Legal — agreed on 13-month retention for enterprise audit events.
2026-03-10: Prototype latency benchmarks look promising (median 1.6ms with cache).
